compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## testing_mode: RED

## Task

Add RED-phase tests to `tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-pr.sh` that verify the multi-tier priority loop behavior of `_phase_remediate`. These tests must fail before T4 (GREEN) implementation.

## Tests to add

### Multi-tier loop behavior
- `t_phase_remediate_skips_to_tier2_when_tier1_artifact_missing`:
  Given: state file with failed_run_id; gh run download succeeds but yields no reviewer-findings.json; _normalize_tier1 exits 3; _normalize_tier2 succeeds
  When: _phase_remediate called
  Then: _dispatch_fix_agent called once (with tier2 output), git push called, returns 0 after repoll succeeds

- `t_phase_remediate_all_tiers_missing_returns_2`:
  Given: all normalizers exit 3 (ARTIFACT_MISSING)
  When: _phase_remediate called
  Then: returns 2 (no tiers produced fixes)

- `t_phase_remediate_continues_to_next_tier_after_repoll_fail`:
  Given: tier1 normalizes successfully; dispatch succeeds; push succeeds; _phase_poll returns 1 (CI still failing); tier2 normalizes successfully; tier2 dispatch + push + repoll succeeds
  When: _phase_remediate called
  Then: returns 0 (tier2 fixed CI after tier1 fix didn't)

- `t_phase_remediate_tier1_success_does_not_try_tier2`:
  Given: tier1 normalizes, dispatches, pushes, and repoll returns 0
  When: _phase_remediate called
  Then: _normalize_tier2 never called; returns 0

## Test setup pattern
- Use the same pattern as existing _phase_remediate tests:
  - Stub functions (gh, git, _dispatch_fix_agent, _phase_poll, _normalize_tier1/_tier2) via bash function override
  - Set state file with `_state_record_failed_run_id` written to temp state file
  - Set MERGE_STRATEGY=pr, BRANCH=test-multitier-$, PR_LIB_MODE=1 in subshell
  - Use call_counter pattern to verify function call ordering
- RED marker: add '[t_phase_remediate_skips_to_tier2_when_tier1_artifact_missing]' to .test-index for merge-to-main-pr.sh

## Files to modify
- tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-pr.sh
- .test-index (add RED marker)
